   124	/-- A line polynomial evaluates to `a` at `u` when `u` has a line parameter
   125	and every such parameter gives the same value.  The universal clause handles
   126	the zero-direction presentation without choosing a sentinel parameter. -/
   127	def EvaluatesTo {L : LdParams} {c : ℕ} (line : LineDesc L)
   128	    (f : DegPoly L c) (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) (a : ScalarQ L) : Prop :=
   129	  (∃ t : ScalarQ L, u = line.base + t • line.direction) ∧
   130	    ∀ t : ScalarQ L, u = line.base + t • line.direction → degPolyEval f t = a
   131	
   132	/-- Partially evaluate a line polynomial at a point. The value is undefined
   133	when the point does not determine an evaluation. This formalization-only
   134	completion is used in blueprint chapter 14; the displayed family at paper
   135	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:197-206` has no bottom outcome. -/
   136	noncomputable def evalOpt {L : LdParams} {c : ℕ} (line : LineDesc L)
   137	    (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) (f : DegPoly L c) : Option (ScalarQ L) := by
   138	  classical
   139	  exact if h : ∃ a : ScalarQ L, EvaluatesTo line f u a then
   140	    some (Classical.choose h)
   141	  else none
   142	
   143	/-- Convert an axis-line CL output to its seed-bearing presentation; paper
   144	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:243-257,276-287`. -/
   145	def aLineDescOf (L : LdParams) (line : LdSpace L) : LineDesc L :=
   146	  let direction := coordinateDirection (chiIndex L line.seed)
   147	  let base := lineRepMap direction line.point
   148	  LineDesc.axis base line.seed (lineRepMap_apply_self direction line.point)
   149	
   150	/-- Convert a diagonal-line CL output to its seed-bearing presentation; paper
   151	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:261-287`. -/
   152	def dLineDescOf (L : LdParams) (line : LdSpace L) : LineDesc L :=
   153	  let direction := prefixProjection (chiIndex L line.seed) line.direction
   154	  let base := lineRepMap direction line.point
   155	  LineDesc.diagonal base line.seed direction
   156	    (lineRepMap_apply_self direction line.point) (by
   157	      intro j hj
   158	      change prefixProjection (chiIndex L line.seed) line.direction j = 0
   159	      rw [prefixProjection, if_pos hj])
   160	
   161	/-- The axis-line/point component of the low-degree line-point sampler; paper
   162	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:243-257,274-287`. -/
   163	noncomputable def aLinePointDist (L : LdParams) :
   164	    Distribution (LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) :=
   165	  (clDistribution (ldALineCL L) (ldPointCL L)).map fun sample =>
   166	    (aLineDescOf L sample.1, LdSpace.point sample.2)
   167	
   168	/-- The diagonal-line/point component of the low-degree line-point sampler; paper
   169	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:261-287`. -/
   170	noncomputable def dLinePointDist (L : LdParams) :
   171	    Distribution (LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) :=
   172	  (clDistribution (ldDLineCL L) (ldPointCL L)).map fun sample =>
   173	    (dLineDescOf L sample.1, LdSpace.point sample.2)
   174	
   175	/-- The equal mixture of axis and diagonal line-point samples from
   176	`def:line-point-dist`; paper
   177	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:274-287`. -/
   178	noncomputable def linePointDist (L : LdParams) :
   179	    Distribution (LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) :=
   180	  Distribution.mix (1 / 2) (by norm_num) (by norm_num)
   181	    (aLinePointDist L) (dLinePointDist L)
   182	
   183	/-- The affine line-point component has total probability one. -/
   184	theorem aLinePointDist_isProbability (L : LdParams) :
   185	    (aLinePointDist L).IsProbability := by
   186	  sorry
   187	
   188	/-- The diagonal line-point component has total probability one. -/
   189	theorem dLinePointDist_isProbability (L : LdParams) :
   190	    (dLinePointDist L).IsProbability := by
   191	  sorry
   192	
   193	/-- The line-point mixture has total probability one. -/
   194	theorem linePointDist_isProbability (L : LdParams) :
   195	    (linePointDist L).IsProbability := by
   196	  exact Distribution.mix_isProbability _ _ _
   197	    (aLinePointDist_isProbability L) (dLinePointDist_isProbability L)
   198	    (by norm_num) (by norm_num)
   199	
   200	end
   201

    58	/-- The observable associated with a binary measurement; formalization-only notation
    59	used in `thm:ms-from-ac`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:251-261`, paper
    60	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:658-722`. -/
    61	def obsOf {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    62	    (M : Measurement (ZMod 2) ι) : Op ι :=
    63	  M.effect 0 - M.effect 1
    64	
    65	/-- The ideal two-qubit projector for one Magic Square output bit. The other
    66	qubit is marginalized by summing the two-qubit Pauli basis projectors. -/
    67	noncomputable def idealMagicBitProj (W : PauliKind) (b : ZMod 2) :
    68	    Op (Fin 2 → ZMod 2) :=
    69	  ∑ e : Fin 2 → ZMod 2, if e 0 = b then pauliProj W e else 0
    70	
    71	/-- The ideal state in `thm:ms-rigidity`: two EPR pairs followed by the
    72	auxiliary bipartite state, in local-player register order. -/
    73	noncomputable def idealMsState {ιA'' ιB'' : Type*}
    74	    [Fintype ιA''] [DecidableEq ιA''] [Fintype ιB''] [DecidableEq ιB'']
    75	    (aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA'' × ιB'')) :
    76	    EuclideanSpace ℂ
    77	      (((Fin 2 → ZMod 2) × ιA'') × ((Fin 2 → ZMod 2) × ιB'')) :=
    78	  reindexState prodShuffle (vecTensor (eprState (Fin 2 → ZMod 2)) aux)
    79	
    80	/-- The isometries and auxiliary unit state in the conclusion of
    81	`thm:ms-rigidity`. -/
    82	structure MsRigidityWitness (S : Strategy msGame) where
    83	  ιA'' : Type
    84	  ιB'' : Type
    85	  [ιA''Fintype : Fintype ιA'']
    86	  [ιB''Fintype : Fintype ιB'']
    87	  [ιA''DecidableEq : DecidableEq ιA'']
    88	  [ιB''DecidableEq : DecidableEq ιB'']
    89	  φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
    90	    EuclideanSpace ℂ ((Fin 2 → ZMod 2) × ιA'')
    91	  φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
    92	    EuclideanSpace ℂ ((Fin 2 → ZMod 2) × ιB'')
    93	  aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA'' × ιB'')
    94	  aux_norm : ‖aux‖ = 1
    95	
    96	attribute [instance] MsRigidityWitness.ιA''Fintype
    97	  MsRigidityWitness.ιB''Fintype MsRigidityWitness.ιA''DecidableEq
    98	  MsRigidityWitness.ιB''DecidableEq
    99	
   100	/-- Alice's bit-measurement distance in `thm:ms-rigidity`. -/
   101	noncomputable def msOperatorDistanceA (S : Strategy msGame)
   102	    (w : MsRigidityWitness S) (j : Fin 9) (W : PauliKind) : ℝ :=
   103	  opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution Unit)
   104	    (fun _ b => heteroKron
   105	      (conjIsometry w.φA
   106	        (((S.A (.var j)).postprocess msBitOrZero).effect b)) 1)
   107	    (fun _ b => heteroKron
   108	      (heteroKron (idealMagicBitProj W b) (1 : Op w.ιA'')) 1)
   109	    (idealMsState w.aux)
   110	
   111	/-- Bob's bit-measurement distance in `thm:ms-rigidity`. -/
   112	noncomputable def msOperatorDistanceB (S : Strategy msGame)
   113	    (w : MsRigidityWitness S) (j : Fin 9) (W : PauliKind) : ℝ :=
   114	  opFamilyDistSq (uniformDistribution Unit)
   115	    (fun _ b => heteroKron 1
   116	      (conjIsometry w.φB
   117	        (((S.B (.var j)).postprocess msBitOrZero).effect b)))
   118	    (fun _ b => heteroKron 1
   119	      (heteroKron (idealMagicBitProj W b) (1 : Op w.ιB'')))
   120	    (idealMsState w.aux)
   121	
   122	/-- Alice's anticommutator defect from the consequence in
   123	`thm:ms-rigidity`. -/
   124	noncomputable def msAnticommutatorDistanceA (S : Strategy msGame)
   125	    (w : MsRigidityWitness S) : ℝ :=
   126	  let X := heteroKron
   127	    (conjIsometry w.φA (obsOf ((S.A (.var 0)).postprocess msBitOrZero))) 1
   128	  let Z := heteroKron
   129	    (conjIsometry w.φA (obsOf ((S.A (.var 4)).postprocess msBitOrZero))) 1
   130	  opDistSq (uniformDistribution Unit) (fun _ => X * Z)
   131	    (fun _ => -(Z * X)) (idealMsState w.aux)
   132	
   133	/-- Bob's anticommutator defect from the consequence in
   134	`thm:ms-rigidity`. -/
   135	noncomputable def msAnticommutatorDistanceB (S : Strategy msGame)
   136	    (w : MsRigidityWitness S) : ℝ :=
   137	  let X := heteroKron 1
   138	    (conjIsometry w.φB (obsOf ((S.B (.var 0)).postprocess msBitOrZero)))
   139	  let Z := heteroKron 1
   140	    (conjIsometry w.φB (obsOf ((S.B (.var 4)).postprocess msBitOrZero)))
   141	  opDistSq (uniformDistribution Unit) (fun _ => X * Z)
   142	    (fun _ => -(Z * X)) (idealMsState w.aux)
   143	
   144	/-- `thm:ms-rigidity`, imported from Coladangelo--Stark, Theorem 6.9.
   145	Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:222-244`, paper
   146	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:612-652`.
   147	
   148	The paper states the Euclidean estimate at scale `sqrt ε` at lines 624--626
   149	and explains the norm conversion and local basis change at lines 650--652. One
   150	universal constant applies to every strategy and nonnegative error parameter. -/
   151	theorem exists_ms_rigidity :
   152	    ∃ C : ℝ, 1 ≤ C ∧ ∀ (ε : ℝ), 0 ≤ ε →
   153	      ∀ S : Strategy msGame, 1 - ε ≤ S.value →
   154	        ∃ w : MsRigidityWitness S,
   155	          ‖isometryTensor w.φA w.φB S.ψ - idealMsState w.aux‖ ≤
   156	              C * Real.sqrt ε ∧
   157	          msOperatorDistanceA S w 0 .X ≤ C * Real.sqrt ε ∧
   158	          msOperatorDistanceA S w 4 .Z ≤ C * Real.sqrt ε ∧
   159	          msOperatorDistanceB S w 0 .X ≤ C * Real.sqrt ε ∧
   160	          msOperatorDistanceB S w 4 .Z ≤ C * Real.sqrt ε ∧
   161	          msAnticommutatorDistanceA S w ≤ C * Real.sqrt ε ∧
   162	          msAnticommutatorDistanceB S w ≤ C * Real.sqrt ε := by
   163	  sorry
   164	
   165	/-- The state of the perfect strategy constructed in `thm:ms-from-ac`. -/
   166	noncomputable def msPerfectState (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   167	    [Nonempty ι] : EuclideanSpace ℂ ((ι × ZMod 2) × (ι × ZMod 2)) :=
   168	  reindexState prodShuffle (vecTensor (eprState ι) (eprState (ZMod 2)))
   169	
   170	/-- `thm:ms-from-ac`: any anticommuting pair of projective binary
   171	measurements, consistent on an EPR state, extends to a value-one SPCC Magic
   172	Square strategy. Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:251-261`, paper
   173	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:654-722`.
   174	
   175	The local index type is arbitrary, finite, and nonempty; no field model or QPBT
   176	parameter is assumed. The equality `hι` identifies the target local Hilbert
   177	space with the constructed tensor factor. -/
   178	theorem exists_ms_perfect_strategy_of_anticommuting
   179	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι]
   180	    (A B : Measurement (ZMod 2) ι)
   181	    (hA : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective A)
   182	    (hB : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective B)
   183	    (hcA : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsConsistentOn A (eprState ι))
   184	    (hcB : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsConsistentOn B (eprState ι))
   185	    (hac : obsOf A * obsOf B = -(obsOf B * obsOf A)) :
   186	    ∃ S : SymmetricStrategy msGameSymm, ∃ hι : S.ι = (ι × ZMod 2),
   187	      S.IsSPCC ∧ S.toStrategy.value = 1 ∧
   188	      reindexState (Equiv.prodCongr (Equiv.cast hι) (Equiv.cast hι)) S.ψ =
   189	        msPerfectState ι ∧
   190	      ∀ b : ZMod 2,
   191	        reindexOp (Equiv.cast hι.symm) ((S.M (.var 0)).effect (.bit b)) =
   192	            heteroKron (A.effect b) (1 : Op (ZMod 2)) ∧
   193	          reindexOp (Equiv.cast hι.symm) ((S.M (.var 4)).effect (.bit b)) =
   194	            heteroKron (B.effect b) (1 : Op (ZMod 2)) := by
   195	  sorry

   197	end

     4	/-!
     5	# Qubit form of Pauli basis test soundness
     6	
     7	The fixed self-dual normal basis converts the qudit EPR register and generalized
     8	Pauli projectors into qubit coordinates. The conversion uses only the basis
     9	stored in the canonical `FixedFieldModel`.
    10	
    11	## References
    12	
    13	The conversion is `lem:pauli-binary` in
    14	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:710-741`, from
    15	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1163-1208`. The resulting
    16	`cor:pauli-binary` is in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:430-454`,
    17	from `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1450-1491`.
    18	-/
    19	
    20	open scoped BigOperators Matrix
    21	
    22	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    23	
    24	open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.Quantum
    25	
    26	noncomputable section
    27	
    28	/-- The bit register obtained by expanding every Pauli-register field element
    29	in the basis stored by `P.model`. -/
    30	abbrev QubitRegister (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
    31	  Cube P.m × Fin P.model.basisDim → ZMod 2
    32	
    33	/-- The ideal auxiliary state tensored with the qubit EPR register, in the
    34	local-player ordering used by `cor:pauli-binary`. -/
    35	noncomputable def idealQubitState (P : AdmissibleParams)
    36	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
    37	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
    38	    (aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × ιB')) :
    39	    EuclideanSpace ℂ
    40	      ((ιA' × QubitRegister P) × (ιB' × QubitRegister P)) :=
    41	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv
    42	      ((ιA' × QubitRegister P) × (ιB' × QubitRegister P)) ℂ).symm
    43	    (fun p =>
    44	      (EuclideanSpace.equiv (ιA' × ιB') ℂ aux (p.1.1, p.2.1)) *
    45	        (EuclideanSpace.equiv (QubitRegister P × QubitRegister P) ℂ
    46	          (eprState (QubitRegister P)) (p.1.2, p.2.2)))
    47	
    48	/-- The local isometries, auxiliary spaces, and unit auxiliary state in
    49	`cor:pauli-binary`; this structure introduces no hypothesis beyond the paper
    50	theorem. -/
    51	structure QubitSoundnessWitness (P : AdmissibleParams)
    52	    (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P)) where
    53	  ιA' : Type
    54	  ιB' : Type
    55	  [ιAFintype : Fintype ιA']
    56	  [ιBFintype : Fintype ιB']
    57	  [ιADecidableEq : DecidableEq ιA']
    58	  [ιBDecidableEq : DecidableEq ιB']
    59	  φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
    60	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × QubitRegister P)
    61	  φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
    62	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιB' × QubitRegister P)
    63	  aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × ιB')
    64	  aux_norm : ‖aux‖ = 1
    65	
    66	attribute [instance] QubitSoundnessWitness.ιAFintype
    67	  QubitSoundnessWitness.ιBFintype QubitSoundnessWitness.ιADecidableEq
    68	  QubitSoundnessWitness.ιBDecidableEq
    69	
    70	/-- Alice's ideal qubit projector placed on the joint target space. -/
    71	noncomputable def qubitProjOnA'' (P : AdmissibleParams)
    72	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
    73	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB'] (W : PauliKind)
    74	    (u : PauliRegister P) :
    75	    Op ((ιA' × QubitRegister P) × (ιB' × QubitRegister P)) :=
    76	  fun p q =>
    77	    if p.1.1 = q.1.1 ∧ p.2 = q.2 then
    78	      qubitPauliProj W (kappaVec P.model u) p.1.2 q.1.2
    79	    else 0
    80	
    81	/-- Bob's ideal qubit projector placed on the joint target space. -/
    82	noncomputable def qubitProjOnB'' (P : AdmissibleParams)
    83	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
    84	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB'] (W : PauliKind)
    85	    (u : PauliRegister P) :
    86	    Op ((ιA' × QubitRegister P) × (ιB' × QubitRegister P)) :=
    87	  fun p q =>
    88	    if p.1 = q.1 ∧ p.2.1 = q.2.1 then
    89	      qubitPauliProj W (kappaVec P.model u) p.2.2 q.2.2
    90	    else 0
    91	
    92	/-- Lift a conjugated Alice effect to the full qubit target space. -/
    93	noncomputable def liftedQubitAEffect {P : AdmissibleParams} {G : Game}
    94	    (S : Strategy G) {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
    95	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
    96	    (φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
    97	      EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × QubitRegister P))
    98	    (M : Op S.ιA) :
    99	    Op ((ιA' × QubitRegister P) × (ιB' × QubitRegister P)) :=
   100	  heteroKron (conjIsometry φA M) 1
   101	
   102	/-- Lift a conjugated Bob effect to the full qubit target space. -/
   103	noncomputable def liftedQubitBEffect {P : AdmissibleParams} {G : Game}
   104	    (S : Strategy G) {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
   105	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
   106	    (φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   107	      EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιB' × QubitRegister P))
   108	    (M : Op S.ιB) :
   109	    Op ((ιA' × QubitRegister P) × (ιB' × QubitRegister P)) :=
   110	  heteroKron 1 (conjIsometry φB M)
   111	
   112	/-- Alice's qubit-projector family distance in `cor:pauli-binary`. -/
   113	noncomputable def qubitOperatorDistanceA
   114	    (P : AdmissibleParams) (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P))
   115	    (w : QubitSoundnessWitness P S) (W : PauliKind) : ℝ :=
   116	  ∑ u : PauliRegister P,
   117	    ‖applyOperatorToState
   118	      (liftedQubitAEffect S w.φA
   119	          (((S.A (pauliQuestion P W)).postprocess pauliAnswerOrZero).effect u) -
   120	        qubitProjOnA'' P W u)
   121	      (idealQubitState P w.aux)‖ ^ 2
   122	
   123	/-- Bob's qubit-projector family distance in `cor:pauli-binary`. -/
   124	noncomputable def qubitOperatorDistanceB
   125	    (P : AdmissibleParams) (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P))
   126	    (w : QubitSoundnessWitness P S) (W : PauliKind) : ℝ :=
   127	  ∑ u : PauliRegister P,
   128	    ‖applyOperatorToState
   129	      (liftedQubitBEffect S w.φB
   130	          (((S.B (pauliQuestion P W)).postprocess pauliAnswerOrZero).effect u) -
   131	        qubitProjOnB'' P W u)
   132	      (idealQubitState P w.aux)‖ ^ 2
   133	
   134	/-- `cor:pauli-binary`: soundness of the Pauli basis test in qubit
   135	coordinates. Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:430-454`, paper
   136	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1450-1491`.
   137	
   138	The theorem assumes a nonnegative error parameter, as in the source, and uses
   139	only `P.model` and its stored basis dimension. -/
   140	theorem pauli_soundness_qubit :
   141	    ∃ a b : ℝ, 1 ≤ a ∧ 0 < b ∧ b < 1 ∧
   142	      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε : ℝ), 0 ≤ ε →
   143	        ∀ S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P), 1 - ε ≤ S.value →

  1426	\paragraph{Soundness of the Pauli basis test.} 
  1427	We state the soundness properties of the Pauli basis test.
  1428	The following is an adaptation of the self-testing statement in~\cite[Theorem
  1429	6.4]{NW19}.

  1431	\begin{theorem}
  1432	  \label{thm:pauli}
  1433	There exists a function 
  1434	\[\delta_{\qld}(\eps,m,d,q) = a(md)^a(\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})\]
  1435	 for universal constants $a \geq 1$ and $0 < b < 1$ such that the following holds. For all admissible parameter tuples $\qldparams = (q,m,d)$ and for all strategies $\strategy = (\ket{\psi},A,B)$ for the game $\game^\pauli_\qldparams$ that succeed with probability at least $1 - \eps$, there exist local isometries $\phi_\alice: \mH_\alice \to \mH_{\alice'} \otimes \mH_{\alice''},\phi_\bob: \mH_\bob \to \mH_{\bob'} \otimes \mH_{\bob''}$ (where $\ket{\psi} \in \mH_\alice \otimes \mH_\bob$ and $\mH_{\alice''},\mH_{\bob''} \cong (\C^q)^{\otimes M}$ with $M = 2^m$) and a state $\ket{\aux} \in \mH_{\alice'} \otimes \mH_{\bob'}$ such that 
  1436	\begin{enumerate}
  1437	    \item $\left \| \phi_\alice \otimes \phi_B \ket{\psi} - \ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes M}  \right \| \leq \delta_{\qld}(\eps,m,d,q)$,
  1438	    \item Letting $\tilde{A}^x_a = \phi_A\, A^x_a \, \phi_A^\dagger$ and $\tilde{B}^y_b = \phi_B B^y_b \phi_B^\dagger$, we have for $W \in \{X,Z\}$
  1439	    \begin{gather*}
  1440	        \tilde{A}^{(\pauli,W)}_u \otimes I_{\bob'\bob''} \approx_{\delta_{\qld}} (\tau^W_u)_{\alice''} \otimes I_{\alice' \bob' \bob''} \\
  1441	        I_{\alice'\alice''} \otimes \tilde{B}^{(\pauli,W)}_u    \approx_{\delta_{\qld}} I_{\alice' \alice'' \bob'} \otimes (\tau^W_u)_{\bob''}\;,
  1442	    \end{gather*}
  1443	    where the $\approx_{\delta_{\qld}}$ statement holds with respect to the state $\ket{\aux}_{\alice'\bob'} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes M}_{\alice''\bob''}$ and the answer summation is over $u \in \F_q^M$.
  1444	\end{enumerate}

  1492	\subsubsection{Canonical parameters and complexity of the Pauli basis test}
  1493	\label{sec:qld-complexity}
  1494	
  1495	We specify a canonical setting of the parameter tuple $\qldparams$ as a function
  1496	of an integer $R$.
  1497	We call this canonical setting $\introparams$ because we use these in the
  1498	``introspection'' section (\Cref{sec:introspection}).
  1499	We then give bounds on the complexity of computing the decision procedure and CL
  1500	functions of the Pauli basis test corresponding to the parameter tuple
  1501	$\qldparams$, as a function of $R$.
  1502	
  1503	\begin{definition}[Canonical parameters of the Pauli basis test]
  1504	  \label{def:introparams}
  1505	  Let $a,b$ be the universal constants specified in Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli}.
  1506	  Let $c$ denote the smallest even integer that is at least $(b + a)/b$.
  1507	  For all integers $R \geq 4$, define the tuple $\introparams(R) = (q,m,d)$
  1508	  where
  1509	  \begin{itemize}
  1510	  	\item $q = 2^k$ for $k = c \lceil  \log \log R  \rceil + 1$.
  1511		\item $m = 2^j$ where $2^j \leq c \lceil \log R \rceil + 1 < 2^{j+1}$. 
  1512		\item $d = 1$. 
  1513	  \end{itemize}
  1514	\end{definition}
  1515	
  1516	Intuitively, this choice of parameters is such that the Pauli basis test
  1517	certifies the presence of an $M=2^m$-qudit EPR state (of local dimension $q$), or
  1518	equivalently an $M\log q$-qubit EPR state.
  1519	
  1520	\begin{lemma}
  1521	  \label{lem:delta-bound}
  1522	 For all integers $R \geq 4$, the parameter tuple $\introparams(R) = (q,m,d)$ is
  1523	  admissible (see Definition~\ref{def:admissible}), satisfies $2^m \geq R$, and furthermore there exist
  1524	  universal constants $a'\geq 1$ and $0 < b' \leq 1$ such that the function
  1525	  $\delta_\qld(\eps, m, d, q)$ from Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli} is at most
  1526	   \[
  1527	   	a' ( \log(R)^{a'} \cdot \eps^{b'} + \log(R)^{-b'}) \;.
  1528		\]
  1529	\end{lemma}
  1530	
  1531	\begin{proof}
  1532	  We verify the admissibility of $\introparams(R)$ first: the field size $q =
  1533	  2^k$ is admissible because $k$ is odd. We have $m | q$ because for all $R \geq 4$ we have  
  1534	  \[
  1535	  	2^j \leq 2 c \lceil \log R \rceil \leq 2 \log^c R \leq 2^k~.
  1536	  \]
  1537		Next, we show that $R \leq 2^m$. Since $m = 2^j \geq (c/2) \log R$, we have that
  1538		\[
  1539			2^m \geq R^{c/2} \geq R
  1540		\]
  1541		where we used that $c \geq 2$. 
  1542	
  1543	Finally, we show the desired bound on the error function $\delta_\qld(\eps,m,d,q)$. First, observe that $2^{-bmd} \leq q^{-b}$ because $k \leq m$.
  1544	  Note that for $R \geq 2$, we have $m \leq 2c \log R$, and furthermore $q =
  1545	  2^k \geq \log^c R$.
  1546	Then, we get
  1547	\begin{align*}
  1548	  	\delta_\qld(\eps,m,d,q)
  1549	    & = a (md)^a (\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd}) \tag{by Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli}}  \\
  1550	    & \leq a (md)^a (\eps^b + 2q^{-b}) \tag{because  $2^{-bmd} \leq q^{-b}$}  \\
  1551	    & = a (m)^a (\eps^b + 2q^{-b}) \tag{because  $d=1$}  \\
  1552	    & \leq a (2c)^a \log^{a} (R) ( \eps^{b} + 2q^{-b}) \tag{because  $m \leq 2c \log R$}\\
  1553	    & \leq a (2c)^a \log^{a} (R) ( \eps^{b} + 2(\log R)^{-cb}) \tag{because  $q \geq \log^c R$}\\
  1554	    & \leq 2a (2c)^a \log^{a} (R) ( \eps^{b} + (\log R)^{-cb}) \\
  1555	    & = 2a (2c)^a ( (\log R)^{a}\eps^{b} + (\log R)^{a-cb}) \\
  1556	    & \leq 2a(2c)^{a} \left ( (\log R)^{a} \eps^{b}
  1557	      + (\log R)^{-b} \right) \tag{because  $cb - a \geq b \geq 0$}\\
  1558	    & \leq a' ( (\log R)^{a'} \eps^{b} + (\log R)^{-b}),
  1559	  \end{align*}
  1560	  where $a'$ is defined as the quantity $2a(2c)^a$.
  1561	This completes the proof of the lemma.
  1562	\end{proof}
  1563	
  1564	\begin{lemma}
  1565		\label{lem:introparams-complexity}
  1566		Fix an integer $R \geq 4$, let $\introparams(R) = (q,m,d)$.
  1567		The integers $(q,m,d) = \introparams(R)$ can be computed in time $\polylog
  1568	  R$ when given the binary representation of $R$ as input.
  1569	\end{lemma}
  1570	\begin{proof}
  1571	  This follows from the definitions of the parameters in
  1572	  Definition~\ref{def:introparams}.
  1573	  
  1574	\end{proof}

   394	We define a special class of measurements that are relevant to the soundness
   395	properties of the low-degree test.
   396	
   397	\begin{definition}[Low-degree polynomial measurements]
   398	  \label{def:ld-meas}
   399	  Define $\polymeas{m}{d}{q}$ to be the set of POVM measurements whose outcomes
   400	  correspond to (individual) degree-$d$ polynomials of $m$ variables over
   401	  $\F_q$.
   402	  More generally, for an integer $\ldc$ and tuples $m=(m_1, m_2, \ldots,
   403	  m_\ldc)$, $d=(d_1, d_2, \ldots, d_\ldc)$ and $q=(q_1, q_2, \ldots, q_\ldc)$,
   404	  we let $\simulpolymeas{m}{d}{q}{\ldc}$ be the set of measurements $G =
   405	  \{G_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots\,,\, g_\ldc}\}$ such that for $i\in\{1, 2, \ldots,
   406	  \ldc\}$, $g_i$ is a polynomial $g_i:\F_{q_i}^{m_i} \rightarrow
   407	  \F_{q_i}$ with individual degree $d_i$ (see \Cref{sec:ld-encoding} for a definition of individual degree). 
   408	\end{definition}
   409	
   410	Quantum soundness of a version of the classical low-degree test for polynomials of low \emph{total} degree was claimed
   411	in~\cite{natarajan2018low}, building on an analysis of a three-prover version of the test in~\cite{vidick2016three}. Unfortunately there is a gap in the soundness analysis of this test. For our construction we use the low individual degree test, whose quantum soundness is shown in~\cite{ML20} and generalized in~\cite{ji2021quantum}. We state the result in the form that is most directly useful for us, and show how the stated result follows from~\cite{ji2021quantum}.
   412	
   413	\begin{theorem}[Quantum soundness of the simultaneous classical low-degree test]
   414	  \label{lem:ld-soundness}
   415	  There exists a function $\delta_{\ld}(\eps, q, m, d, \ldc) = a (dm \ldc)^a (\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$ for universal constants $a\geq 1$ and $0<b\leq 1$ 
   416	such that the following
   417	  holds.
   418	  For all $\eps > 0$ and parameter tuple $\ldparams = (q, m, d, \ldc)$, for all
   419	  projective strategies $(\psi,A,B)$ that succeed with probability at least
   420	  $1-\eps$ in the game $\game^\ld_\ldparams$, there exists measurements
   421	  \[G^w \in \simulpolymeas{m}{d}{q}{\ldc}\] on $\mH_w$, for
   422	  $w\in\{\alice,\bob\}$, such that
   423	  \begin{equation*}
   424	    \begin{split}
   425	      A^{\Point,\, u}_{a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots\,,\, a_\ldc}
   426	      & \abc[\delta_{\ld}]
   427	      G^\bob_{[(g_1(u),g_2(u),\ldots,g_\ldc(u)) = (a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots \,,\, a_\ldc)]}\;,\\
   428	      G^\alice_{[(g_1(u),g_2(u),\ldots,g_\ldc(u)) = (a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots \,,\, a_\ldc)]}
   429	      & \abc[\delta_{\ld}]
   430				 B^{\Point,\, u}_{a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots\,,\, a_\ldc}\;,\\
   431	      G^\alice_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots \,,\, g_\ldc}
   432	      & \abc[\delta_{\ld}]
   433	      G^\bob_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots \,,\, g_\ldc}\;,
   434	    \end{split}
   435	  \end{equation*}
   436	  where $\delta_{\ld} = \delta_{\ld}(\eps, q, m, d, \ldc)$, 
   437	  and all three statements are with respect to the state $\ket{\psi}$.
   438	In addition, the first two approximations hold under the uniform distribution over $u\in \F_q^m$,
   439		whereas there is no question distribution associated with the third approximation.
   440	\end{theorem}
   441	
   442	\begin{proof}
   443	Let $\ldparams = (q, m, d, \ldc)$
   444	where $m, d, \ldc \in \N$ are integers, $q \in \N$ is an admissible field size,
   445	and $m$ divides $q$. Let $\Sigma=\F_q$. Let $\code \subseteq \Sigma^q$ be the Reed-Solomon code with degree $d$. Explicitly, $\code$ is the set of all $(p(x_1),\ldots,p(x_n))$ where $p:\F_q\to\F_q$ is a univariate polynomial of degree at most $d$ and $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ are an enumeration of $\F_q$. Then in the (standard) notation from~\cite{ji2021quantum} $\code$ is a linear $[q,d+1,n-d+1]_\Sigma$ code.
   446	
   447	Observe that the two-prover tensor code test, for the code $\code^{\otimes m}$, as described in~\cite[Figure 1 and Figure 2]{ji2021quantum}, is identical to the game $\game^\ld$ with parameters $\ldparams$ and $\ldc=1$, whose decider is presented in Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider}. This is because 
   448	\begin{enumerate}
   449	\item The \emph{axis-parallel line-versus-point test} from Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} is identical to the \emph{axis-parallel lines test} from~\cite[Figure 1]{ji2021quantum}, with the only difference that in Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} the roles of A and B are chosen uniformly at random. This is consistent with the two-prover variant of the tensor code test from~\cite[Section 4.1]{ji2021quantum}.
   450	\item The \emph{diagonal line-versus-point test} from Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} is identical to the \emph{subcube commutation test} from~\cite[Figure 1]{ji2021quantum}, with again the added symmetrization between players. 
   451	\item The \emph{consistency test} from Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} is identical to the \emph{synchronicity test} from~\cite[Figure 2]{ji2021quantum}.
   452	\end{enumerate}
   453	
   454	As a result,~\cite[Theorem 4.7]{ji2021quantum}, in which we choose the parameter $k$ as $k=m^3d$,  immediately yields \Cref{lem:ld-soundness}.
   455	
   456	To conclude it remains to extend the result to the case of general $\ldc$. This is done 
   457	via a standard reduction, following exactly the same steps as the derivation of Theorem 4.43 from Theorem 4.40 in~\cite{NW19}.
   458	\end{proof}

   465	\subsubsection{Complexity of the classical low-degree test.}
   466	The CL functions and decision procedure of the low-degree test are incorporated
   467	as subroutines in some of the normal form verifiers constructed in subsequent
   468	sections.
   469	The next lemma establishes the time complexity of these procedures as a function
   470	of the parameter tuple $\ldparams = (q,m,d,k)$.
   471	The lemma also establishes the time complexity of computing the {description} of
   472	the decision procedure $\decider^\ld$ as a Turing machine, given the parameter
   473	tuple $\ldparams$ as input.
   474	
   475	
   476	
   477	\begin{lemma}[Complexity of the classical low-degree test]
   478	  \label{lem:ld-complexity}
   479	  Let $\ldparams = (q,m,d,k)$ denote a parameter tuple.
   480	  \begin{enumerate}
   481		\item The time complexity of the decision procedure $\decider^\ld$
   482	    parametrized by $\ldparams$ is $\poly(m, d, k, \log q)$.
   483		\item The time complexity of evaluating marginals of the CL functions
   484	    $L_\Point$, $L_\ALine$, and $L_\DLine$ at a given input point is $\poly(m, \log
   485	    q)$.
   486		\item The Turing machine description of the decision procedure $\decider^\ld$
   487	    parametrized by $\ldparams$ can be computed from $\ldparams$ in $\polylog
   488	    (q,m,d,k)$ time.
   489	  \end{enumerate}
   490	\end{lemma}
   491	
   492	\begin{proof}
   493		Finite field arithmetic over $\F_q$ can be performed in time $\polylog q$, by
   494	  Lemma~\ref{lem:efficient_arithmetic}.
   495		The most expensive step in $\decider^\ld$ is to evaluate a univariate
   496	  polynomial $f: \F_q \to \F_q^k$ at some point $t_u \in \F_q$ that corresponds
   497	  to a point $u \in \F_q^m$, which takes time $\poly(m,d,k,\log q)$.
   498	  The function $L_\Point$ is a projection onto $V_\xpt$, which takes time
   499	  $\poly(m,\log q)$ to compute (it just involves ``zeroing out'' the registers
   500	  outside of $V_\xpt$).

   612	The following theorem records the self-testing (also known as \emph{rigidity})
   613	properties of the Magic Square game.
   614	Its self-testing properties
   615	are crucial to the Pauli basis test.
   616	In particular, it is used to enforce anticommutation relations between certain
   617	pairs of operators.
   618	We will refer to this theorem in the proof of the soundness of the Pauli basis test (\Cref{thm:pauli} below) in \Cref{sec:qld-analysis}.
   619	
   620	\begin{theorem}[Rigidity of the Magic Square game]
   621	  \label{thm:ms-rigidity}
   622	
   623	
   624	Let $\strategy = (\ket{\psi},A,B)$ be a strategy that succeeds in the Magic Square game $\game^{\MS}$ with probability $1 - \eps$, where $\ket{\psi} \in \mH_A \otimes \mH_B$ is a state. Then there exist local isometries $\phi_A: \mH_A \to \mH_{A'} \otimes \mH_{A''},\phi_B: \mH_B \to \mH_{B'} \otimes \mH_{B''}$ (where $\mH_{A'},\mH_{B'} \cong (\C^2)^{\otimes 2}$ and $\mH_{A''},\mH_{B''}$ are finite dimensional) and a state $\ket{\aux} \in \mH_{A''} \otimes \mH_{B''}$ such that 
   625	\begin{enumerate}
   626	    \item $\left \| \phi_A \otimes \phi_B \ket{\psi} - \ket{\EPR_2}^{\otimes 2} \otimes \ket{\aux} \right \| \leq O(\sqrt{\eps})$,
   627	    \item Letting $\tilde{A}^x_a = \phi_A\, A^x_a \, \phi_A^\dagger$ and $\tilde{B}^y_b = \phi_B B^y_b \phi_B^\dagger$, we have that
   628	    \begin{gather*}
   629	        \tilde{A}^{\Variable_1}_b \otimes I_{B'B''} \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} (\sigma^X_b)_{A'} \otimes I_{A'' B' B''} \\
   630	        \tilde{A}^{\Variable_5}_b \otimes I_{B'B''} \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} (\sigma^Z_b)_{A'} \otimes I_{A'' B' B''} \\
   631	        I_{A'A''} \otimes \tilde{B}^{\Variable_1}_b    \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} I_{A' A'' B''} \otimes (\sigma^X_b)_{B'} \\
   632	        I_{A'A''} \otimes \tilde{B}^{\Variable_5}_b    \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} I_{A' A'' B''} \otimes (\sigma^Z_b)_{B'}
   633	    \end{gather*}
   634	    where the $\approx_{\sqrt{\eps}}$ statement holds with respect to the state $\ket{\EPR_2}^{\otimes 2}_{A'B'} \otimes \ket{\aux}_{A''B''}$ and the answer summation is over $b \in \{0,1\}$. As a consequence, letting 
   635	    \begin{gather*}
   636	    \tilde{A}^{\Variable_1} = \tilde{A}^{\Variable_1}_0 - \tilde{A}^{\Variable_1}_1 \\
   637	    \tilde{A}^{\Variable_5} = \tilde{A}^{\Variable_5}_0 - \tilde{A}^{\Variable_5}_1 \\
   638	    \end{gather*}
   639	    it holds that
   640	    \begin{gather*}
   641	        \tilde{A}^{\Variable_1} \tilde{A}^{\Variable_5} \otimes I_{B' B''} \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} - \tilde{A}^{\Variable_5}  \tilde{A}^{\Variable_1} \otimes I_{B' B''} \\
   642	        I_{A' A''} \otimes \tilde{B}^{\Variable_1} \tilde{B}^{\Variable_5}  \approx_{\sqrt{\eps}} - I_{A' A''} \otimes \tilde{B}^{\Variable_5}  \tilde{B}^{\Variable_1} \;,
   643	      \end{gather*}
   644	      where the notation $M \approx_{\delta} N$ for $M, N$ that are not POVM
   645	      elements means
   646	      \[  \bra{\psi} (M-N)^\dagger (M-N) \ket{\psi}  \leq  O(\delta). \]
   647	\end{enumerate}
   648	
   649	\end{theorem}
   650	\begin{proof}
   651	 	A proof of the rigidity of the Magic Square game can be found in~\cite[Theorem 6.9]{coladangelo2017robust}. There are a couple minor differences between their rigidity statement and the one stated here. First, they state that the robustness of the Magic Square self-test is $O(\eps)$; however they specify the closeness between the actual and ideal states in terms of the trace norm, whereas we specify the closeness between $\phi_\alice \otimes \phi_\bob \ket{\psi}$ and $\ket{\EPR_2}^{\otimes 2}\otimes \ket{\aux}$ in terms of the Euclidean distance, which translates to $O(\sqrt{\eps})$ instead of $O(\eps)$. Second, their choice of ideal strategy specifies that the observables corresponding to $\Variable_1$ and $\Variable_5$ questions are $I \otimes \sigma^Z$ and $\sigma^{Z} \sigma^{X} \otimes \sigma^Z \sigma^X$; however under a local change of basis these are equivalent to $\sigma^X \otimes I$ and $\sigma^Z \otimes I$ respectively.
   652	\end{proof}
   653	
   654	We will need the following theorem,
   655	which shows that any pair of anticommuting observables 
   656	can be used to form a value-$1$ strategy for the Magic Square game.
   657	
   658	\begin{theorem}
   659	  \label{thm:ms-from-ac}
   660	  Let $A = \{A_b\}_{b \in \F_2}$ and $B = \{B_b\}_{b \in \F_2}$ be two-outcome
   661	  projective measurements acting on $(\C^q)^{\otimes n}$ which are consistent on
   662	  $\ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes n}$, and let $\mathcal{O}_A = A_0 - A_1$ and
   663	  $\mathcal{O}_B = B_0 - B_1$ be the corresponding observables.
   664	  Suppose that $\mathcal{O}_A \mathcal{O}_B = -\mathcal{O}_B \mathcal{O}_A$.
   665	  Then there exists a symmetric strategy $\strategy = (\psi, M)$ for the Magic
   666	  Square game with the following properties.
   667	  \begin{enumerate}
   668	  \item $\strategy$ is an SPCC strategy of value $1$.
   669	  \item The state $\ket{\psi}$ has the form $\ket{\psi} = \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes
   670	      n} \otimes \ket{\EPR_2}$.
   671	  \item For $b \in \{0,1\}$, we have $M^{\Variable_1}_b = A_b \otimes I$ and
   672	    $M^{\Variable_5}_b = B_b \otimes I$.\label{item:embeds}
   673	  \end{enumerate}
   674	\end{theorem}
   675	
   676	\begin{proof}
   677	  The strategy~$\strategy$ is based on the canonical two-qubit strategy for the
   678	  Magic Square game as described in, for example,~\cite{aravind2002simple}.
   679	  The state is $\ket{\psi} = \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes n} \otimes \ket{\EPR_2}$.
   680	  We specify the measurements of~$\strategy$ in
   681	  Figure~\ref{fig:ms-operator-soln} as an \emph{operator solution} for the Magic
   682	  Square game, meant to be read as follows: each cell contains a two-outcome
   683	  projective measurement $\{E_0, E_1\}$ on $(\C^q)^{\otimes n} \otimes \C^2$
   684	  written as its \emph{$\pm 1$-valued observable} $E_0 - E_1$.
   685	  When Player~$\alice$ or~$\bob$ receives the question $\Variable_j$ for $j \in
   686	  \{1, \ldots, 9\}$, they measure their share of~$\ket{\psi}$ using the
   687	  measurement specified by the cell corresponding to~$\Variable_j$ and receive a
   688	  single-bit measurement.
   689	  When they receive the question $\Constraint_i$ for $i \in \{1,2,\ldots,6\}$,
   690	  they simultaneously perform the three measurements in the corresponding row or
   691	  column on $\ket{\psi}$ to obtain three bits.
   692	  For example, if Player~$\alice$ receives question~$\Variable_1$, they
   693	  measure~$\ket{\psi}$ using the measurement $\{A_0 \otimes I, A_1 \otimes I\}$
   694	  corresponding to the observable $\cal{O}_A \otimes I$ (where the first
   695	  operator acts on $\ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes n}$ and the second acts on
   696	  $\ket{\EPR_2}$).
   697	  Similarly, on question~$\Variable_5$, they use the measurement $\{B_0 \otimes
   698	  I, B_1 \otimes I\}$.
   699	  This establishes Item~\ref{item:embeds} of the theorem.

   144	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:243-257,276-287`. -/
   145	def aLineDescOf (L : LdParams) (line : LdSpace L) : LineDesc L :=
   146	  let direction := coordinateDirection (chiIndex L line.seed)
   147	  let base := lineRepMap direction line.point
   148	  LineDesc.axis base line.seed (lineRepMap_apply_self direction line.point)
   149	
   150	/-- Convert a diagonal-line CL output to its seed-bearing presentation; paper
   151	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:261-287`. -/
   152	def dLineDescOf (L : LdParams) (line : LdSpace L) : LineDesc L :=
   153	  let direction := prefixProjection (chiIndex L line.seed) line.direction
   154	  let base := lineRepMap direction line.point
   155	  LineDesc.diagonal base line.seed direction
   156	    (lineRepMap_apply_self direction line.point) (by
   157	      intro j hj
   158	      change prefixProjection (chiIndex L line.seed) line.direction j = 0
   159	      rw [prefixProjection, if_pos hj])
   160	
   161	/-- The axis-line/point component of the low-degree line-point sampler; paper
   162	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:243-257,274-287`. -/
   163	noncomputable def aLinePointDist (L : LdParams) :
   164	    Distribution (LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) :=
   165	  (clDistribution (ldALineCL L) (ldPointCL L)).map fun sample =>
   166	    (aLineDescOf L sample.1, LdSpace.point sample.2)
   167	
   168	/-- The diagonal-line/point component of the low-degree line-point sampler; paper
   169	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:261-287`. -/
   170	noncomputable def dLinePointDist (L : LdParams) :
   171	    Distribution (LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) :=
   172	  (clDistribution (ldDLineCL L) (ldPointCL L)).map fun sample =>
   173	    (dLineDescOf L sample.1, LdSpace.point sample.2)
   174	
   175	/-- The equal mixture of axis and diagonal line-point samples from
   176	`def:line-point-dist`; paper
   177	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:274-287`. -/
   178	noncomputable def linePointDist (L : LdParams) :
   179	    Distribution (LineDesc L × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) :=
   180	  Distribution.mix (1 / 2) (by norm_num) (by norm_num)
   181	    (aLinePointDist L) (dLinePointDist L)
   182	
   183	/-- The affine line-point component has total probability one. -/
   184	theorem aLinePointDist_isProbability (L : LdParams) :
   185	    (aLinePointDist L).IsProbability := by
   186	  sorry
   187	
   188	/-- The diagonal line-point component has total probability one. -/
   189	theorem dLinePointDist_isProbability (L : LdParams) :
   190	    (dLinePointDist L).IsProbability := by
   191	  sorry
   192	
   193	/-- The line-point mixture has total probability one. -/
   194	theorem linePointDist_isProbability (L : LdParams) :
   195	    (linePointDist L).IsProbability := by
   196	  exact Distribution.mix_isProbability _ _ _
   197	    (aLinePointDist_isProbability L) (dLinePointDist_isProbability L)
   198	    (by norm_num) (by norm_num)
   199	
   200	end
   201	
   202	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     6	/-!
     7	# Low-degree polynomial measurements and soundness
     8	
     9	This file defines the finite polynomial-measurement index and states the
    10	low-degree soundness theorem used by the QPBT combining argument. Polynomial
    11	outcomes are bounded multivariate polynomials.
    12	
    13	## References
    14	
    15	The principal definition and theorem are `def:ld-meas` and `lem:ld-soundness` in
    16	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:63-160`. Their paper origin is
    17	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:243-287,392-480`.
    18	The dimension-divisibility hypothesis is documented in
    19	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`.
    20	-/
    21	
    22	open scoped BigOperators
    23	
    24	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    25	
    26	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    27	open MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries
    28	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    29	
    30	noncomputable section
    31	
    32	/-- The positive dimension in `LdParams` supplies the finite coordinate type
    33	used by the uniform axis and prefix-index marginals. -/
    34	instance (L : LdParams) : Nonempty (Fin L.m) :=
    35	  ⟨⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one L.hm⟩⟩
    36	
    37	/-- `lem:alnf`: the point and axis-index marginals of the axis line-point
    38	distribution are uniform. Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:63-68`, paper
    39	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:243-257`. -/
    40	theorem aLinePointDist_point_marginal_uniform (L : LdParams) :
    41	    (aLinePointDist L).map Prod.snd =
    42	        uniformDistribution (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) ∧
    43	      (aLinePointDist L).map (fun sample => chiIndex L sample.1.seed) =
    44	        uniformDistribution (Fin L.m) := by
    45	  sorry
    46	
    47	/-- The incidence conclusion of `lem:alnf`, blueprint
    48	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:63-68`, paper
    49	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:243-257`. -/
    50	theorem aLinePointDist_mem_line (L : LdParams) :
    51	    ∀ sample ∈ (aLinePointDist L).support, sample.2 ∈ sample.1.pointSet := by
    52	  sorry
    53	
    54	/-- `lem:dlnf`: the point and prefix-index marginals of the diagonal
    55	line-point distribution are uniform. Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:74-79`,
    56	paper `08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:261-272`. -/
    57	theorem dLinePointDist_point_marginal_uniform (L : LdParams) :
    58	    (dLinePointDist L).map Prod.snd =
    59	        uniformDistribution (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) ∧
    60	      (dLinePointDist L).map (fun sample => chiIndex L sample.1.seed) =
    61	        uniformDistribution (Fin L.m) := by
    62	  sorry
    63	
    64	/-- The incidence conclusion of `lem:dlnf`, blueprint
    65	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:74-79`, paper
    66	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:261-272`. -/
    67	theorem dLinePointDist_mem_line (L : LdParams) :
    68	    ∀ sample ∈ (dLinePointDist L).support, sample.2 ∈ sample.1.pointSet := by
    69	  sorry
    70	
    71	/-- The diagonal direction in every sampled description has the prefix-zero
    72	property of `lem:dlnf`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:74-79`, paper
    73	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:261-272`. -/
    74	theorem dLinePointDist_prefix_zero (L : LdParams) :
    75	    ∀ sample ∈ (dLinePointDist L).support,
    76	      ∀ j : Fin L.m, j.val < (chiIndex L sample.1.seed).val →
    77	        sample.1.direction j = 0 := by
    78	  sorry
    79	
    80	/-- The low-degree question sampler is the typed conditionally linear
    81	distribution on the complete type graph. This identifies the sampler with
    82	`def:typed-cl-distributions`; blueprint
    83	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:624-629`, paper
    84	`references/qpbt-paper/07_types.tex:84-94`. -/
    85	theorem ldQuestionDistribution_eq_typedCL (L : LdParams) :
    86	    ldQuestionDistribution L =
    87	      typedCLDistribution (Finset.univ : Finset (Sym2 LdType)) (by simp)
    88	        (ldCL L) (ldCL L) := by
    89	  sorry
    90	
    91	/-- Bounded multivariate polynomials form a finite set over a finite coefficient
    92	semiring. This is the finite outcome set required by `def:ld-meas`,
    93	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:124-129`, paper
    94	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:394-408`. -/
    95	noncomputable instance polyFuncFintype (m : ℕ) (K : Type*)
    96	    [CommSemiring K] [Fintype K] (d : ℕ) : Fintype ↥(polyFunc m K d) := by
    97	  letI : Finite ↥(polyFunc m K d) := Module.finite_of_finite K
    98	  exact Fintype.ofFinite _
    99	
   100	/-- A bounded multivariate polynomial outcome over an arbitrary finite
   101	coefficient semiring. -/
   102	noncomputable abbrev PolyIndex (m : ℕ) (K : Type*) [CommSemiring K]
   103	    [Fintype K] (d : ℕ) := ↥(polyFunc m K d)
   104	
   105	/-- A POVM indexed by one bounded multivariate polynomial. -/
   106	noncomputable abbrev PolyMeas (m : ℕ) (K : Type*) [CommSemiring K]
   107	    [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K] (d : ℕ) (ι : Type*)
   108	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] := Measurement (PolyIndex m K d) ι
   109	
   110	/-- The dependent family in `def:ld-meas`: component `i` may
   111	have its own coefficient field, number of variables, and degree bound.
   112	Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:124-129`, paper
   113	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:394-408`. -/
   114	noncomputable abbrev PolyMeasFamily (k : ℕ) (K : Fin k → Type*)
   115	    [∀ i, CommSemiring (K i)] [∀ i, Fintype (K i)]
   116	    [∀ i, DecidableEq (K i)] (m d : Fin k → ℕ) (ι : Type*)
   117	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] :=
   118	  Measurement ((i : Fin k) → PolyIndex (m i) (K i) (d i)) ι
   119	
   120	/-- A simultaneous tuple of `L.k` bounded polynomial representatives. -/
   121	noncomputable abbrev PolyTuple (L : LdParams) :=
   122	  Fin L.k → PolyIndex L.m (ScalarQ L) L.d
   123	
   124	/-- The constant-family specialization used by `lem:ld-soundness`. -/
   125	noncomputable abbrev PolyMeasTuple (L : LdParams) (ι : Type*)
   126	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] :=
   127	  PolyMeasFamily L.k (fun _ => ScalarQ L) (fun _ => L.m) (fun _ => L.d) ι
   128	
   129	/-- Evaluate every component of a polynomial tuple at a point. -/
   130	def evalPolyTupleAt {L : LdParams} (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)
   131	    (g : PolyTuple L) : Fin L.k → ScalarQ L :=
   132	  fun j => MvPolynomial.eval u (g j).1
   133	
   134	/-- Embed a geometric point into the ambient coefficient space used by a
   135	point question. -/
   136	def pointSpaceOf (L : LdParams) (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) : LdSpace L :=
   137	  fun i => match i with
   138	  | .inl (.inl j) => u j
   139	  | .inl (.inr _) => 0
   140	  | .inr _ => 0
   141	
   142	/-- The typed low-degree point question associated with `u`. -/
   143	def ldPointQuestionOf (L : LdParams) (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) : LdQuestion L :=
   144	  (.point, pointSpaceOf L u)
   145	
   146	/-- Read the point component of a low-degree answer, sending answers of the
   147	wrong form to the fixed zero tuple. This total relabeling turns the strategy's
   148	answer measurement into the point POVM used by `lem:ld-soundness`. -/
   149	def ldPointValuesOrZero (L : LdParams) : LdAnswer L → Fin L.k → ScalarQ L
   150	  | .pointVals values => values
   151	  | .alinePolys _ => 0
   152	  | .dlinePolys _ => 0
   153	
   154	/-- The quantitative error function in `lem:ld-soundness`.  Its argument order
   155	is `(a, b, ε, q, m, d, k)`. -/
   156	noncomputable def deltaLd (a b ε : ℝ) (q m d k : ℕ) : ℝ :=
   157	  a * Real.rpow (((d * m * k : ℕ) : ℝ)) a *
   158	    (Real.rpow ε b + Real.rpow (q : ℝ) (-b) +
   159	      Real.rpow 2 (-(b * ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ))))
   160	
   161	/-- Quantum soundness of the simultaneous classical low individual degree
   162	test (`lem:ld-soundness`, blueprint lines 135--160; paper theorem and proof
   163	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:413-458`).
   164	
   165	The first two consistency bounds compare the point-answer postprocessing of the
   166	strategy with evaluations of the polynomial measurements. Answers of the wrong
   167	form are folded into the zero tuple so that the point family remains a POVM.
   168	
   169	The source reduction still requires proofs of the claimed game correspondence
   170	and of the auxiliary parameter bound. These two open facts are detailed in
   171	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex` and
   172	`rem:ld-soundness-provider`, and are tracked by issue #16. -/
   173	theorem exists_ld_soundness :
   174	    ∃ a b : ℝ, 1 ≤ a ∧ 0 < b ∧ b ≤ 1 ∧
   175	      ∀ (L : LdParams) (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε →
   176	        ∀ S : Strategy (ldGame L), S.IsProjective → 1 - ε ≤ S.value →
   177	          ∃ GA : PolyMeasTuple L S.ιA, ∃ GB : PolyMeasTuple L S.ιB,
   178	            consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L))
   179	                (fun u outcome =>
   180	                  heteroKron
   181	                    (((S.A (ldPointQuestionOf L u)).postprocess
   182	                      (ldPointValuesOrZero L)).effect outcome) 1)
   183	                (fun u outcome =>
   184	                  heteroKron 1
   185	                    ((GB.postprocess (evalPolyTupleAt u)).effect outcome))
   186	                S.ψ ≤ deltaLd a b ε L.q L.m L.d L.k ∧
   187	            consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L))
   188	                (fun u outcome =>
   189	                  heteroKron
   190	                    ((GA.postprocess (evalPolyTupleAt u)).effect outcome) 1)
   191	                (fun u outcome =>
   192	                  heteroKron 1
   193	                    (((S.B (ldPointQuestionOf L u)).postprocess
   194	                      (ldPointValuesOrZero L)).effect outcome))
   195	                S.ψ ≤ deltaLd a b ε L.q L.m L.d L.k ∧
   196	            consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Unit)
   197	                (fun _ g => heteroKron (GA.effect g) 1)
   198	                (fun _ g => heteroKron 1 (GB.effect g))
   199	                S.ψ ≤ deltaLd a b ε L.q L.m L.d L.k := by
   200	  sorry
   201	
   202	end
   203	
   204	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

1	import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Test.PauliBasisTest

     4	/-!
     5	# Pauli basis test soundness
     6	
     7	The quantitative error function and the source-shaped soundness statement live
     8	here.  All analytic estimates are intentionally proof-level obligations in the
     9	stage-4.1 skeleton; the carriers below are concrete finite-dimensional vectors
    10	and matrices so that later proofs can use the existing Hilbert-space API.
    11	
    12	## References
    13	
    14	The main declaration is `thm:pauli` in
    15	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:407-424`, with paper origin
    16	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
    17	The distance functionals use `def:state-distance` and `def:povm-distance` from
    18	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:187-226`.
    19	-/
    20	
    21	open scoped BigOperators Matrix ComplexOrder
    22	
    23	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    24	
    25	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    26	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    27	
    28	noncomputable section
    29	
    30	/-- The Pauli-test error scale.  The argument order is `(a, b, ε, m, d, q)`;
    31	the powers are real `rpow`s and the asymptotic constants are absorbed into `a`,
    32	as specified by `thm:pauli` (`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:407-424`,
    33	paper `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`).
    34	-/
    35	noncomputable def deltaQld (a b ε : ℝ) (m d q : ℕ) : ℝ :=
    36	  a * Real.rpow ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ) a *
    37	    (Real.rpow ε b + Real.rpow (q : ℝ) (-b) +
    38	      Real.rpow 2 (-(b * ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ))))
    39	
    40	/-- The ideal auxiliary state `aux ⊗ EPR_q^{⊗M}` in the shuffled register
    41	ordering.  The EPR factor is the concrete `eprState` from
    42	`def:EPR` (`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:537-547`; paper
    43	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:946-955`).
    44	-/
    45	noncomputable def idealState (P : AdmissibleParams)
    46	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
    47	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
    48	    (aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × ιB')) :
    49	    EuclideanSpace ℂ ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
    50	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) ×
    51	      (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) ℂ).symm
    52	    (fun p =>
    53	      ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (ιA' × ιB') ℂ) aux (p.1.1, p.2.1)) *
    54	        ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P) ℂ)
    55	          (eprState (PauliRegister P)) (p.1.2, p.2.2)))
    56	
    57	/-- The Pauli question carrying no additional coefficient data, as in
    58	`def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:350-386`, paper origin
    59	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1006-1008`.
    60	-/
    61	def pauliQuestion (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind) : PauliQuestion P :=
    62	  (.pauli W, 0)
    63	
    64	/-- The A-side ideal Pauli projector, with identities on the auxiliary and
    65	B-side registers.  This is a concrete matrix form of the operator comparison
    66	in `thm:pauli` (`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:407-424`; paper
    67	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`).
    68	-/
    69	noncomputable def pauliProjOnA'' (P : AdmissibleParams)
    70	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
    71	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB'] (W : PauliKind)
    72	    (u : PauliRegister P) :
    73	    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
    74	  fun p q =>
    75	    if p.1.1 = q.1.1 ∧ p.2 = q.2 then
    76	      pauliProj W u p.1.2 q.1.2
    77	    else 0
    78	
    79	/-- The symmetric B-side ideal Pauli projector from `thm:pauli`, blueprint
    80	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:407-424`, paper origin
    81	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
    82	-/
    83	noncomputable def pauliProjOnB'' (P : AdmissibleParams)
    84	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
    85	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB'] (W : PauliKind)
    86	    (u : PauliRegister P) :
    87	    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
    88	  fun p q =>
    89	    if p.1 = q.1 ∧ p.2.1 = q.2.1 then
    90	      pauliProj W u p.2.2 q.2.2
    91	    else 0
    92	
    93	/-- Lift a conjugated A-side effect to the full ideal register in `thm:pauli`,
    94	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:407-424`, paper origin
    95	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
    96	-/
    97	noncomputable def liftedAEffect {P : AdmissibleParams} {G : Game}
    98	    (S : Strategy G) {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
    99	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
   100	    (φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   101	      EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × PauliRegister P))
   102	    (M : Op S.ιA) :
   103	    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
   104	  fun p q =>
   105	    if p.2 = q.2 then
   106	      (conjIsometry φA M) p.1 q.1
   107	    else 0
   108	
   109	/-- Lift a conjugated B-side effect to the full ideal register in `thm:pauli`,
   110	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:407-424`, paper origin
   111	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
   112	-/
   113	noncomputable def liftedBEffect {P : AdmissibleParams} {G : Game}
   114	    (S : Strategy G) {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
   115	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
   116	    (φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   117	      EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιB' × PauliRegister P))
   118	    (M : Op S.ιB) :
   119	    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
   120	  fun p q =>
   121	    if p.1 = q.1 then
   122	      (conjIsometry φB M) p.2 q.2
   123	    else 0
   124	
   125	/-- A finite witness packaging the auxiliary dimensions, isometries, and state
   126	from `thm:pauli`.  This structure is a Lean-only encoding of the existential
   127	data in the paper theorem; it introduces no extra hypothesis.  Blueprint
   128	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:407-424`, paper origin
   129	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
   130	-/
   131	structure PauliSoundnessWitness (P : AdmissibleParams)
   132	    (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P)) where
   133	  ιA' : Type
   134	  ιB' : Type
   135	  [ιAFintype : Fintype ιA']
   136	  [ιBFintype : Fintype ιB']
   137	  [ιADecidableEq : DecidableEq ιA']
   138	  [ιBDecidableEq : DecidableEq ιB']
   139	  φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   140	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × PauliRegister P)
   141	  φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   142	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιB' × PauliRegister P)
   143	  aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × ιB')
   144	  aux_norm : ‖aux‖ = 1
   145	
   146	attribute [instance] PauliSoundnessWitness.ιAFintype PauliSoundnessWitness.ιBFintype
   147	  PauliSoundnessWitness.ιADecidableEq PauliSoundnessWitness.ιBDecidableEq
   148	
   149	/-- The A-side operator-distance quantity appearing in the soundness
   150	conclusion.  It is the finite-sum realization of `def:povm-distance` from
   151	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:219-226`, paper origin
   152	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:258-271`.
   153	-/
   154	noncomputable def pauliOperatorDistanceA
   155	    (P : AdmissibleParams) (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P))
   156	    (w : PauliSoundnessWitness P S) (W : PauliKind) : ℝ :=
   157	  ∑ u : PauliRegister P,
   158	      ‖applyOperatorToState (liftedAEffect S w.φA
   159	        (((S.A (pauliQuestion P W)).postprocess pauliAnswerOrZero).effect u) -

    43		the field is clear from context we write $\mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}$, and when

   182		By the definition of the indicator vector
   183		(Definition~\ref{def:indicator-vector}), expanding the product over the
   184		coordinates $i \in \{1, \dots, m\}$ into a sum over $y \in \{0,1\}^m$
   185		gives
   186		\[
   187			\mathrm{ind}_m(u_X) \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(u_Z)
   188			\,=\, \sum_{y \in \{0,1\}^m} \mathrm{ind}_{m,y}(u_X)\, \mathrm{ind}_{m,y}(u_Z)
   189			\,=\, \prod_{i=1}^{m} \big( u_{X,i}\, u_{Z,i} + (1 - u_{X,i})(1 - u_{Z,i}) \big)\,,
   190		\]
   191		and since $\F_q$ has characteristic $2$, the $i$-th factor equals
   192		$1 + u_{X,i} + u_{Z,i}$. Hence
   193		\[
   194			\gamma(\omega) \,=\, \tr\Big( (r_X r_Z) \cdot \prod_{i=1}^{m} (1 + u_{X,i} + u_{Z,i}) \Big)\,.
   195		\]
   196		For any fixed $u_X$, the $m$ factors $1 + u_{X,i} + u_{Z,i}$ are
   197		independent and uniformly distributed in $\F_q$ over the choice of
   198		$u_Z$, so all of them are nonzero with probability $(1-q^{-1})^m$;
   199		independently, $r_X \neq 0$ with probability $1 - q^{-1}$. If $r_X = 0$
   200		or some factor vanishes, then $\gamma(\omega) = 0$. Otherwise, over the
   201		uniform choice of $r_Z$, the argument of the trace is a uniformly random
   202		element of $\F_q$. Since $q = 2^k$ is admissible, the trace of an
   203		element of $\F_q$ equals the coordinate sum of its binary
   204		representation: writing $\kappa$ for the binary representation with
   205		respect to the fixed self-dual normal basis
   206		(Definition~\ref{def:binary-representation}), item~2 of
   207		Lemma~\ref{lem:downsize_field} gives
   208		$\tr(c) = \tr(c \cdot 1) = \kappa(c) \cdot \kappa(1)$, and $\kappa(1)$
   209		is the all-ones vector by Lemma~\ref{lem:one}. As $\kappa$ is a
   210		bijection onto $\F_2^k$, a uniformly random element of $\F_q$ has trace
   211		$0$ with probability exactly $\frac12$. Combining, the probability that
   212		$\gamma(\omega) \neq 0$ is exactly $(1-q^{-1})^{m+1} \cdot \frac12$, and
   213		the probability that $\omega$ is commuting is the complement, which is
   214		at least $\frac12$.
   215	
   216		If $m \leq q$, then
   217		$(1-q^{-1})^{m+1} \geq (1-q^{-1})^{q+1} = (1-q^{-1})^{q} \cdot (1-q^{-1})$,
   218		a product of two positive functions of $q$ that are nondecreasing for
   219		$q \geq 2$, so it is minimized at $q = 2$, where it equals $2^{-3}$;
   220		hence the anticommuting probability is at least $2^{-4}$.

43:+    lineRepMap v (lineRepMap v u) = lineRepMap v u := by

56:+An axis description stores its canonical base and seed. A diagonal description

263:+`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1520-1562`. -/
264:+theorem introParamsTuple_isAdmissible (a b : ℝ) (R : ℕ) (hR : 4 ≤ R) :
265:+    IsAdmissibleTuple (introParamsTuple (introParamsC a b) R) := by
266:+  sorry
268:+/-- The canonical admissible parameter structure of `def:introparams`,
269:+blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:471-482`, paper
270:+`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1503-1514`. -/
271:+noncomputable def introParams (a b : ℝ) (R : ℕ) (hR : 4 ≤ R) :
272:+    AdmissibleParams :=
273:+  AdmissibleParams.ofTuple _ (introParamsTuple_isAdmissible a b R hR)
275:+/-- The canonical parameter dimension supplies at least `R` encoded
276:+coordinates, as asserted in `lem:delta-bound`. -/
277:+theorem le_two_pow_introParams_m (a b : ℝ) (ha : 1 ≤ a) (hb : 0 < b)
278:+    (R : ℕ) (hR : 4 ≤ R) :
279:+    R ≤ 2 ^ (introParams a b R hR).m := by
280:+  sorry
282:+/-- `lem:delta-bound`: the Pauli soundness error at the canonical parameters
283:+has polylogarithmic dependence on `R`. Blueprint
284:+`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:484-492`, paper
285:+`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1520-1562`.
287:+**Local fix:** The third error term is bounded directly using the lower bound
288:+on `m`, rather than the source's false intermediate comparison between the
289:+field exponent and `m`. This discrepancy is documented in issue #16 and
290:+`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_delta-bound-exponent-comparison.tex`; see also
291:+`rem:delta-bound-exponent-comparison`. -/
292:+theorem exists_deltaQld_introParams_bound (a b : ℝ) (ha : 1 ≤ a)
293:+    (hb : 0 < b) (hb' : b < 1) :
294:+    ∃ a' b' : ℝ, 1 ≤ a' ∧ 0 < b' ∧ b' ≤ 1 ∧
295:+      ∀ (R : ℕ) (hR : 4 ≤ R) (ε : ℝ),
296:+        deltaQld a b ε (introParams a b R hR).m
297:+            (introParams a b R hR).d (introParams a b R hR).q ≤
298:+          a' * (Real.rpow (Real.logb 2 R) a' * Real.rpow ε b' +
299:+            Real.rpow (Real.logb 2 R) (-b')) := by
300:+  sorry
302:+end
304:+end MIPStarRE.QPBT

317:+/-!
318:+# Completeness of the Pauli basis test
320:+This file presents the Pauli basis test as a symmetric game and states its
321:+value-one SPCC completeness theorem.
323:+## References
325:+The source statement is `lem:pauli-completeness` in
326:+`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:390-395`, from
327:+`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1229-1421`.
328:+-/
330:+namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
332:+noncomputable section
334:+/-- The Pauli question sampler equals the typed conditionally linear distribution
335:+on the Pauli type graph from `def:typed-cl-distributions`; blueprint
336:+`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:624-629`,
337:+paper `references/qpbt-paper/07_types.tex:84-94`. -/
338:+theorem pauliQuestionDistribution_eq_typedCL (P : AdmissibleParams) :
339:+    pauliQuestionDistribution P =
340:+      typedCLDistribution pauliEdges (by
341:+        refine ⟨Sym2.mk (.point .X) (.point .X), ?_⟩
342:+        simp [pauliEdges]) (pauliCL P) (pauliCL P) := by
343:+  sorry
345:+/-- Symmetry of the Pauli question distribution in the symmetric game appearing
346:+in `lem:pauli-completeness`. -/
347:+theorem pauliQuestionDistribution_symm (P : AdmissibleParams)
348:+    (x y : PauliQuestion P) :
349:+    (pauliQuestionDistribution P).weight (x, y) =
350:+      (pauliQuestionDistribution P).weight (y, x) := by
351:+  sorry
353:+/-- Symmetry of the Pauli decision predicate in the symmetric game appearing in
354:+`lem:pauli-completeness`. -/
355:+theorem pauliWinPredicate_symm (P : AdmissibleParams)
356:+    (x y : PauliQuestion P) (a b : PauliAnswer P) :
357:+    pauliWinPredicate P x y a b = pauliWinPredicate P y x b a := by
358:+  sorry
360:+/-- The symmetric presentation of the Pauli basis test. The field and basis
361:+are those fixed by `P.model`; no additional model is quantified. -/
362:+noncomputable def pauliBasisTestSymm (P : AdmissibleParams) : SymmetricGame where
363:+  Question := PauliQuestion P
364:+  Answer := PauliAnswer P
365:+  μ := pauliQuestionDistribution P
366:+  μ_prob := (pauliBasisTest P).μ_prob
367:+  μ_symm := pauliQuestionDistribution_symm P
368:+  decide := pauliWinPredicate P
369:+  decide_symm := pauliWinPredicate_symm P
371:+/-- The symmetric presentation has the Pauli basis test as its
372:+underlying game. -/
373:+theorem pauliBasisTestSymm_toGame (P : AdmissibleParams) :
374:+    (pauliBasisTestSymm P).toGame = pauliBasisTest P := by
375:+  rfl
377:+/-- `lem:pauli-completeness`: every admissible Pauli basis test has a
378:+value-one SPCC strategy. Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:390-395`, paper
379:+`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1229-1421`. -/
380:+theorem exists_spcc_value_one (P : AdmissibleParams) :
381:+    ∃ S : SymmetricStrategy (pauliBasisTestSymm P),
382:+      S.IsSPCC ∧ S.toStrategy.value = 1 := by
383:+  sorry
385:+end
387:+end MIPStarRE.QPBT

399:+/-!
400:+# Low-degree polynomial measurements and soundness
402:+This file defines the finite polynomial-measurement index and states the
403:+low-degree soundness theorem used by the QPBT combining argument. Polynomial
404:+outcomes are bounded multivariate polynomials.
406:+## References
408:+The principal definition and theorem are `def:ld-meas` and `lem:ld-soundness` in
409:+`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:63-160`. Their paper origin is
410:+`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:243-287,392-480`.
411:+The dimension-divisibility hypothesis is documented in
412:+`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`.
413:+-/
415:+open scoped BigOperators
417:+namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
419:+open MIPStarRE.LDT
420:+open MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries
421:+open MIPStarRE.Quantum
423:+noncomputable section
425:+/-- The positive dimension in `LdParams` supplies the finite coordinate type
426:+used by the uniform axis and prefix-index marginals. -/
427:+instance (L : LdParams) : Nonempty (Fin L.m) :=
428:+  ⟨⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one L.hm⟩⟩
430:+/-- `lem:alnf`: the point and axis-index marginals of the axis line-point
431:+distribution are uniform. Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:63-68`, paper
432:+`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:243-257`. -/
433:+theorem aLinePointDist_point_marginal_uniform (L : LdParams) :
434:+    (aLinePointDist L).map Prod.snd =
435:+        uniformDistribution (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) ∧
436:+      (aLinePointDist L).map (fun sample => chiIndex L sample.1.seed) =
437:+        uniformDistribution (Fin L.m) := by
438:+  sorry
440:+/-- The incidence conclusion of `lem:alnf`, blueprint
441:+`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:63-68`, paper
442:+`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:243-257`. -/
443:+theorem aLinePointDist_mem_line (L : LdParams) :
444:+    ∀ sample ∈ (aLinePointDist L).support, sample.2 ∈ sample.1.pointSet := by
445:+  sorry
447:+/-- `lem:dlnf`: the point and prefix-index marginals of the diagonal
448:+line-point distribution are uniform. Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:74-79`,
449:+paper `08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:261-272`. -/
450:+theorem dLinePointDist_point_marginal_uniform (L : LdParams) :
451:+    (dLinePointDist L).map Prod.snd =
452:+        uniformDistribution (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) ∧
453:+      (dLinePointDist L).map (fun sample => chiIndex L sample.1.seed) =
454:+        uniformDistribution (Fin L.m) := by
455:+  sorry
457:+/-- The incidence conclusion of `lem:dlnf`, blueprint
458:+`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:74-79`, paper
459:+`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:261-272`. -/
460:+theorem dLinePointDist_mem_line (L : LdParams) :
461:+    ∀ sample ∈ (dLinePointDist L).support, sample.2 ∈ sample.1.pointSet := by
462:+  sorry
464:+/-- The diagonal direction in every sampled description has the prefix-zero
465:+property of `lem:dlnf`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:74-79`, paper
466:+`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:261-272`. -/
467:+theorem dLinePointDist_prefix_zero (L : LdParams) :
468:+    ∀ sample ∈ (dLinePointDist L).support,
469:+      ∀ j : Fin L.m, j.val < (chiIndex L sample.1.seed).val →
470:+        sample.1.direction j = 0 := by
471:+  sorry
473:+/-- The low-degree question sampler is the typed conditionally linear
474:+distribution on the complete type graph. This identifies the sampler with
475:+`def:typed-cl-distributions`; blueprint
476:+`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:624-629`, paper
477:+`references/qpbt-paper/07_types.tex:84-94`. -/
478:+theorem ldQuestionDistribution_eq_typedCL (L : LdParams) :
479:+    ldQuestionDistribution L =
480:+      typedCLDistribution (Finset.univ : Finset (Sym2 LdType)) (by simp)
481:+        (ldCL L) (ldCL L) := by
482:+  sorry
484:+/-- Bounded multivariate polynomials form a finite set over a finite coefficient
485:+semiring. This is the finite outcome set required by `def:ld-meas`,
486:+blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:124-129`, paper
487:+`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:394-408`. -/
488:+noncomputable instance polyFuncFintype (m : ℕ) (K : Type*)
489:+    [CommSemiring K] [Fintype K] (d : ℕ) : Fintype ↥(polyFunc m K d) := by
490:+  letI : Finite ↥(polyFunc m K d) := Module.finite_of_finite K
491:+  exact Fintype.ofFinite _
493:+/-- A bounded multivariate polynomial outcome over an arbitrary finite
494:+coefficient semiring. -/
495:+noncomputable abbrev PolyIndex (m : ℕ) (K : Type*) [CommSemiring K]
496:+    [Fintype K] (d : ℕ) := ↥(polyFunc m K d)
498:+/-- A POVM indexed by one bounded multivariate polynomial. -/
499:+noncomputable abbrev PolyMeas (m : ℕ) (K : Type*) [CommSemiring K]
500:+    [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K] (d : ℕ) (ι : Type*)
501:+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] := Measurement (PolyIndex m K d) ι
503:+/-- The dependent family in `def:ld-meas`: component `i` may
504:+have its own coefficient field, number of variables, and degree bound.
505:+Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:124-129`, paper
506:+`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:394-408`. -/
507:+noncomputable abbrev PolyMeasFamily (k : ℕ) (K : Fin k → Type*)
508:+    [∀ i, CommSemiring (K i)] [∀ i, Fintype (K i)]
509:+    [∀ i, DecidableEq (K i)] (m d : Fin k → ℕ) (ι : Type*)
510:+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] :=
511:+  Measurement ((i : Fin k) → PolyIndex (m i) (K i) (d i)) ι
513:+/-- A simultaneous tuple of `L.k` bounded polynomial representatives. -/
514:+noncomputable abbrev PolyTuple (L : LdParams) :=
515:+  Fin L.k → PolyIndex L.m (ScalarQ L) L.d
517:+/-- The constant-family specialization used by `lem:ld-soundness`. -/
518:+noncomputable abbrev PolyMeasTuple (L : LdParams) (ι : Type*)
519:+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] :=
520:+  PolyMeasFamily L.k (fun _ => ScalarQ L) (fun _ => L.m) (fun _ => L.d) ι
522:+/-- Evaluate every component of a polynomial tuple at a point. -/
523:+def evalPolyTupleAt {L : LdParams} (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)
524:+    (g : PolyTuple L) : Fin L.k → ScalarQ L :=
525:+  fun j => MvPolynomial.eval u (g j).1
527:+/-- Embed a geometric point into the ambient coefficient space used by a
528:+point question. -/
529:+def pointSpaceOf (L : LdParams) (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) : LdSpace L :=
530:+  fun i => match i with
531:+  | .inl (.inl j) => u j
532:+  | .inl (.inr _) => 0
533:+  | .inr _ => 0
535:+/-- The typed low-degree point question associated with `u`. -/
536:+def ldPointQuestionOf (L : LdParams) (u : Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) : LdQuestion L :=
537:+  (.point, pointSpaceOf L u)
539:+/-- Read the point component of a low-degree answer, sending answers of the
540:+wrong form to the fixed zero tuple. This total relabeling turns the strategy's
541:+answer measurement into the point POVM used by `lem:ld-soundness`. -/
542:+def ldPointValuesOrZero (L : LdParams) : LdAnswer L → Fin L.k → ScalarQ L
543:+  | .pointVals values => values
544:+  | .alinePolys _ => 0
545:+  | .dlinePolys _ => 0
547:+/-- The quantitative error function in `lem:ld-soundness`.  Its argument order
548:+is `(a, b, ε, q, m, d, k)`. -/
549:+noncomputable def deltaLd (a b ε : ℝ) (q m d k : ℕ) : ℝ :=
550:+  a * Real.rpow (((d * m * k : ℕ) : ℝ)) a *
551:+    (Real.rpow ε b + Real.rpow (q : ℝ) (-b) +
552:+      Real.rpow 2 (-(b * ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ))))
554:+/-- Quantum soundness of the simultaneous classical low individual degree
555:+test (`lem:ld-soundness`, blueprint lines 135--160; paper theorem and proof
556:+`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:413-458`).
558:+The first two consistency bounds compare the point-answer postprocessing of the
559:+strategy with evaluations of the polynomial measurements. Answers of the wrong
560:+form are folded into the zero tuple so that the point family remains a POVM.
562:+The source reduction still requires proofs of the claimed game correspondence
563:+and of the auxiliary parameter bound. These two open facts are detailed in
564:+`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex` and
565:+`rem:ld-soundness-provider`, and are tracked by issue #16. -/
566:+theorem exists_ld_soundness :
567:+    ∃ a b : ℝ, 1 ≤ a ∧ 0 < b ∧ b ≤ 1 ∧
568:+      ∀ (L : LdParams) (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε →
569:+        ∀ S : Strategy (ldGame L), S.IsProjective → 1 - ε ≤ S.value →
570:+          ∃ GA : PolyMeasTuple L S.ιA, ∃ GB : PolyMeasTuple L S.ιB,
571:+            consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L))
572:+                (fun u outcome =>
573:+                  heteroKron
574:+                    (((S.A (ldPointQuestionOf L u)).postprocess
575:+                      (ldPointValuesOrZero L)).effect outcome) 1)
576:+                (fun u outcome =>
577:+                  heteroKron 1
578:+                    ((GB.postprocess (evalPolyTupleAt u)).effect outcome))
579:+                S.ψ ≤ deltaLd a b ε L.q L.m L.d L.k ∧
580:+            consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L))
581:+                (fun u outcome =>
582:+                  heteroKron
583:+                    ((GA.postprocess (evalPolyTupleAt u)).effect outcome) 1)
584:+                (fun u outcome =>
585:+                  heteroKron 1
586:+                    (((S.B (ldPointQuestionOf L u)).postprocess
587:+                      (ldPointValuesOrZero L)).effect outcome))
588:+                S.ψ ≤ deltaLd a b ε L.q L.m L.d L.k ∧
589:+            consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Unit)
590:+                (fun _ g => heteroKron (GA.effect g) 1)
591:+                (fun _ g => heteroKron 1 (GB.effect g))
592:+                S.ψ ≤ deltaLd a b ε L.q L.m L.d L.k := by
593:+  sorry
595:+end
597:+end MIPStarRE.QPBT
